limitations: source_revision identifies the original fresh formal processor/API builds at 58faf6d68879e1db92122df493172eab59c02458. The host-only child c9cf9ba0730f236e110a1d48a54d8f47a9faf9af must be bound separately to rebuilt host executables and proven unchanged original kernels/backends; it is not a fresh child backend or RTL build.

This is processor-only rtlsim, which bypasses the AFU. The tensor TFR and scalar STD floating-point paths are native; inherited integer multiply/divide DPI helpers remain. No universal DPI-free processor claim is made.

Only ordinary dense/unscaled FP16/BF16-to-FP32 WMMA under RV64 p02-tfr is covered: one cluster/core, four warps of four threads, issue width one, tile 8x4x8, KUNROLL=1, compact row-major A, column-major B and row-major output.

All 88 processor fixtures use initial FP32 C=+0. K is 8 or 16, with two or four sequential four-product FEDP groups. Tested matrix shapes are 8x4x8, 8x4x16 and 16x8x16. Arbitrary initial C, K>16, long reduction chains, tails, strides, padding, transposition and matrix-load features are outside this processor evidence.

The four K16 numerical cases detect reversal of complete K8 tiles but do not distinguish independently rounded tile partials followed by summation. FP16 range limits make BF16 the source of signed FP32 overflow and output-FTZ coverage; no impossible FP16 overflow sensitivity is implied.

The actual API matrix is RV64 syntax-only C++ in an empty-profile eight-thread configuration with WMMA/WGMMA contexts: 17 successful compiles and 30 expected compiler-exit-1 rejections. Enabled other-format/backend controls establish compatibility only; they do not expand this numerical support scope or establish runtime hardware traps.
